title: Smart Water Metering and Control
headline: Battery-powered retrofit reader that turns existing water meters into smart meters, built on Axino for a client in the Middle East
photoAlt: SciFlair meter reader unit open, showing the sensor node board and battery pack
subtitle: A battery-powered reader that turns existing water meters into connected smart meters, with leak and tamper alerts
need: Water utilities lose revenue to meters that are read by hand, read late or not at all, and to leaks and tampering that go unseen between visits. Replacing every installed meter with a smart meter is costly and slow.
A client in the Middle East asked whether its existing mechanical meters could be read remotely instead, and whether the same network could also control pumps and supply.
role: SciFlair was the design authority. We captured the client's requirements, designed the reader hardware, firmware and head-end software, built the prototypes and tested them on meters in the lab and on site.
built: A retrofit reader that fits existing pulse-output water meters, so the meter itself stays in place
A low-power sensor node board in an IP67 enclosure, running for years on batteries
Our Axino communication module, so the same reader can connect over GSM, LoRa, SigFox, mesh, WiFi or Ethernet to suit each site
Readings stored on the device when the network is down and sent once it returns
Alerts for leaks, continuous flow and tampering
A head-end web application showing every meter on a live map, with consumption history and alarms
Pump and valve control from the same platform, reusing our well pump control design

delivery.title: Concept
delivery.text: Defined the stakeholder requirements with the client and set the measures of performance: battery life, read interval, range and cost per meter.

delivery.title: Architecture
delivery.text: Chose a retrofit architecture on the Axino platform so one reader design could serve different meters and networks.

delivery.title: Design and build
delivery.text: Designed the sensor node board, firmware and enclosure, then built a batch of prototype readers.

delivery.title: Verification
delivery.text: Tested the readers on a range of meter types in our lab and on installed meters on site, verifying reading accuracy, battery drain and radio range.

delivery.title: Next iteration
delivery.text: Fed the results into a smaller, round meter-reader board that fits under the meter cover.
